Done. The pruned checkpoint is written to `out/T2/model.safetensors` and passed on the first execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T2/solution.py` using only safetensors and torch. It loads both input shards through the index file, keeps rows 0..639 and 768..2047 of every q, k and v projection, keeps the same columns of every o_proj, and leaves all other tensors untouched.
- The required checks run as assertions before the write: layer 0 q/k/v are `[1920, 2048]`, o_proj is `[2048, 1920]`, and the tensor count is 114. Extra assertions cover every layer and confirm all dtypes stay float32.
- One execution, no failures.

**Verification**

An independent pass reloaded the output and compared each of the 114 tensors bit-exactly against the sliced input, including dtype and key set. All matched.

**Report**

`out/T2/REPORT.md` lists the tools used and why. I chose direct slicing over transformers `prune_heads` because it avoids instantiating the model, keeps names and dtypes as-is, and is trivially bit-exact.
